content.title: About
content.content: Lima beans are large, pale‑green beans (Phaseolus lunatus) grown in warm climates. In this product they are pre‑cooked, flash‑frozen and enriched with vegetable oil, which enhances flavor and raises caloric value. The beans retain most of the nutrients found in fresh beans.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lima beans are nicknamed “butter beans” because of their creamy texture when cooked.
In nature they mature in flat pods up to 15 cm long.
Freezing preserves over 90 % of vitamin C and most B‑vitamins.
Added oil improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K).
Lima beans are among the oldest cultivated crops, with evidence of use dating back more than 5,000 years in South America.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: One cup (≈170 g) of frozen beans provides about 12 g of protein, making them a solid source for vegetarians.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports normal bowel function and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of potassium and magnesium
items.content: These minerals help regulate blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Fatty acids from added oil
items.content: Vegetable oil supplies energy and aids the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to legumes.

items.title: High caloric density
items.content: The added fat increases the product’s energy content, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Antinutrient content
items.content: Raw beans contain phytic acid, but cooking and freezing dramatically reduce its level.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Beans can cause increased gas in sensitive people; introduce them gradually into the diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Thaw the beans in the refrigerator or under running water, then heat in a skillet, microwave, or add to soups, stews, and salads. They are a convenient quick‑protein addition to fast‑prep meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen beans at –18 °C or lower. After thawing, consume within 2–3 days and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
